question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As life expectancy rises and family structures change, societies are being compelled to rethink how they care ____1____ their ageing populations. In earlier generations, elderly family members typically lived with their children, who assumed responsibility for their welfare as a matter of custom rather than formal arrangement. Today, however, smaller households and migration for work mean that many older adults live alone, ____2____ makes access to healthcare, companionship and financial security far more uncertain. Pension schemes and old-age allowances attempt to provide a measure of economic stability, yet coverage remains uneven, particularly for those who spent their working lives in informal employment. Community-based support networks and assisted-living facilities have therefore begun to ____3____ some of the gaps left by shrinking family care. Policymakers increasingly recognise that dignity in old age depends ____4____ more than income alone; it also requires social connection and accessible healthcare. Building a truly inclusive social security system ____5____ coordinated action from families, communities and the state alike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Care for is the standard collocation meaning to look after or provide for someone's needs, here the needs of ageing populations (की देखभाल करना)

◦ Example: Trained staff are hired to care for patients recovering from surgery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "of" is used in the noun phrase "care of" (e.g. "in the care of"), not with the verb "care" followed by a person, so it does not fit this verb construction.

• Option 3 "with" does not form part of this fixed collocation and sounds unnatural.

• Option 4 "about" would suggest merely feeling concern, not the active sense of looking after someone's needs.

NOTE

• Distinguish care for (to look after) from care about (to feel concern for); the two are not interchangeable.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

As life expectancy rises and family structures change, societies are being compelled to rethink how they care ____1____ their ageing populations. In earlier generations, elderly family members typically lived with their children, who assumed responsibility for their welfare as a matter of custom rather than formal arrangement. Today, however, smaller households and migration for work mean that many older adults live alone, ____2____ makes access to healthcare, companionship and financial security far more uncertain. Pension schemes and old-age allowances attempt to provide a measure of economic stability, yet coverage remains uneven, particularly for those who spent their working lives in informal employment. Community-based support networks and assisted-living facilities have therefore begun to ____3____ some of the gaps left by shrinking family care. Policymakers increasingly recognise that dignity in old age depends ____4____ more than income alone; it also requires social connection and accessible healthcare. Building a truly inclusive social security system ____5____ coordinated action from families, communities and the state alike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. which.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Which correctly introduces a non-restrictive clause here, referring back to the whole preceding idea ("older adults live alone") rather than to a single noun (जो)

◦ Example: He missed the final deadline, which cost the team the entire contract.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "who" is reserved for a specific person as antecedent, not for an entire preceding clause.

• Option 3 "that" is not used to introduce a non-restrictive clause set off by a comma; only "which" is correct in this position.

• Option 4 "whose" indicates possession, which does not fit the intended meaning of "and this makes".

NOTE

• When a relative clause refers back to an entire preceding statement (not a single noun), use which, and always after a comma, never "that".

Pension schemes and old-age allowances attempt to provide a measure of economic stability, yet coverage remains uneven, particularly for those who spent their working lives in informal employment. Community-based support networks and assisted-living facilities have therefore begun to ____3____ some of the gaps left by shrinking family care. Policymakers increasingly recognise that dignity in old age depends ____4____ more than income alone; it also requires social connection and accessible healthcare. Building a truly inclusive social security system ____5____ coordinated action from families, communities and the state alike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fill the gaps is the natural collocation meaning to compensate for something missing, here the support families used to provide (भरना)

◦ Example: Volunteers stepped in to fill the gaps left by the shortage of staff.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "spare" means to give something up for another's use, which does not fit the sense of compensating for an absence.

• Option 3 "exceed" means to go beyond a limit, which is unrelated to compensating for a shortfall.

• Option 4 "restrain" means to hold back or control, which does not fit the sense of addressing a gap in care.

NOTE

• Use the collocation fill the gap(s) to describe compensating for something that is missing or insufficient.

Community-based support networks and assisted-living facilities have therefore begun to ____3____ some of the gaps left by shrinking family care. Policymakers increasingly recognise that dignity in old age depends ____4____ more than income alone; it also requires social connection and accessible healthcare. Building a truly inclusive social security system ____5____ coordinated action from families, communities and the state alike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. on.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Depends on is the fixed collocation meaning determined by or reliant upon, here showing that dignity relies on more than income alone (पर निर्भर करता है)

◦ Example: A team's performance often depends on the quality of its leadership.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "for" is used with other verbs like "account for" or "wait for", not with "depend".

• Option 3 "with" does not form a standard collocation with "depend" in this sense.

• Option 4 "at" is likewise not used with "depend" in standard English.

NOTE

• Memorise the fixed pairing depend on; it cannot be replaced by "for", "with" or "at".

Today, however, smaller households and migration for work mean that many older adults live alone, ____2____ makes access to healthcare, companionship and financial security far more uncertain. Pension schemes and old-age allowances attempt to provide a measure of economic stability, yet coverage remains uneven, particularly for those who spent their working lives in informal employment. Community-based support networks and assisted-living facilities have therefore begun to ____3____ some of the gaps left by shrinking family care. Policymakers increasingly recognise that dignity in old age depends ____4____ more than income alone; it also requires social connection and accessible healthcare. Building a truly inclusive social security system ____5____ coordinated action from families, communities and the state alike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. requires.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Requires agrees with the singular gerund-phrase subject "Building a truly inclusive social security system", which takes a third-person singular verb (आवश्यकता होती है)

◦ Example: Managing a large team requires patience and clear communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "require" is the plural/base form and does not agree with the singular gerund subject.

• Option 3 "are requiring" wrongly uses a plural continuous form with a singular subject and is also stylistically unsuitable for a general truth.

• Option 4 "have required" uses a plural present-perfect auxiliary, again disagreeing with the singular subject.

NOTE

• A gerund phrase (an -ing form acting as a subject, e.g. "Building...") is treated as singular and takes a singular verb.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Every year, millions of workers leave their villages in search of better wages, drawn ____1____ the promise of steady employment in cities. Construction sites, factories and domestic households across urban India depend heavily on this migrant workforce, ____2____ often accept irregular hours and modest pay simply to secure a livelihood. Despite their essential contribution to the urban economy, migrant labourers frequently lack access to affordable housing, healthcare and legal protection, largely because their employment is rarely formalised through written contracts. When economic shocks or public emergencies disrupt city life, these workers are usually the first ____3____ lose their jobs and the last to receive assistance. Policymakers have begun to propose portable welfare benefits that would allow migrants to access healthcare and social security regardless of ____4____ state they are working in. Such reforms, if implemented sincerely, could finally ensure that the people who build and sustain our cities are not treated as ____5____ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• By introduces the agent or cause in a passive construction ("drawn by the promise"), showing what attracts the workers (द्वारा आकर्षित)

◦ Example: Tourists are often drawn by the promise of scenic mountain views.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "with" indicates accompaniment or means, not the cause that draws someone toward something.

• Option 3 "at" does not fit the passive verb "drawn" in this sense.

• Option 4 "through" typically indicates a means or medium, not the direct cause attracting someone.

NOTE

• With passive verbs of attraction such as drawn by / attracted by, the agent is introduced with "by".

Construction sites, factories and domestic households across urban India depend heavily on this migrant workforce, ____2____ often accept irregular hours and modest pay simply to secure a livelihood. Despite their essential contribution to the urban economy, migrant labourers frequently lack access to affordable housing, healthcare and legal protection, largely because their employment is rarely formalised through written contracts. When economic shocks or public emergencies disrupt city life, these workers are usually the first ____3____ lose their jobs and the last to receive assistance. Policymakers have begun to propose portable welfare benefits that would allow migrants to access healthcare and social security regardless of ____4____ state they are working in. Such reforms, if implemented sincerely, could finally ensure that the people who build and sustain our cities are not treated as ____5____ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Who is the correct relative pronoun here because it refers to the people who make up the "migrant workforce", and introduces a clause describing what they do (जो)

◦ Example: The company relies on seasonal workers, who travel from region to region for the harvest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "which" is used for things, not for people, even when the antecedent noun ("workforce") is a collective term for a group of people.

• Option 3 "whom" is the object form and would be needed only if the relative pronoun were the object of the verb, not the subject as it is here ("who... accept").

• Option 4 "whose" indicates possession, which is not the relationship intended in this clause.

NOTE

• When a collective noun (workforce, team, crowd) clearly refers to a group of people acting as the subject of the next clause, use who, not "which".

Such reforms, if implemented sincerely, could finally ensure that the people who build and sustain our cities are not treated as ____5____ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To completes the idiomatic construction "the first to + verb", meaning the earliest ones affected by an action (के लिए)

◦ Example: In any downturn, temporary staff are usually the first to be let go.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "at" does not fit the fixed phrase "the first to do something".

• Option 2 "for" is likewise not used in this construction.

• Option 3 "in" does not complete this idiomatic infinitive structure.

NOTE

• The construction the first/last + to + verb is a fixed pattern used to describe order or sequence of being affected by something.

Read the following passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Every year, millions of workers leave their villages in search of better wages, drawn ____1____ the promise of steady employment in cities. Construction sites, factories and domestic households across urban India depend heavily on this migrant workforce, ____2____ often accept irregular hours and modest pay simply to secure a livelihood. Despite their essential contribution to the urban economy, migrant labourers frequently lack access to affordable housing, healthcare and legal protection, largely because their employment is rarely formalised through written contracts. When economic shocks or public emergencies disrupt city life, these workers are usually the first ____3____ lose their jobs and the last to receive assistance. Policymakers have begun to propose portable welfare benefits that would allow migrants to access healthcare and social security regardless of ____4____ state they are working in. Such reforms, if implemented sincerely, could finally ensure that the people who build and sustain our cities are not treated as ____5____ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. which.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Which correctly completes the phrase "regardless of which state", functioning as an interrogative-style determiner meaning "no matter which" (कौन सा/जो भी)

◦ Example: Everyone deserves fair treatment, regardless of which department they work in.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "that" cannot follow "regardless of" in this determiner sense before a noun like "state".

• Option 3 "this" points to one specific, already-known state, contradicting the general sense of "any state" intended.

• Option 4 "some" would suggest an unspecified single state exists, rather than covering all possible states equally.

NOTE

• The fixed phrase regardless of which/what is used to mean "no matter which one", covering every possibility equally.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. second-class.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Second-class citizens is the standard idiomatic phrase describing people treated as inferior or less deserving of rights than others (द्वितीय श्रेणी के)

◦ Example: Activists argued that the new rule effectively made tenants second-class citizens in their own neighbourhood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "first-rate" means excellent or of the highest quality, the opposite of the intended meaning.

• Option 3 "self-made" describes someone who achieved success through their own effort, unrelated to being treated unfairly.

• Option 4 "well-to-do" means financially prosperous, which is also unrelated to the sense of unequal treatment intended.

NOTE

• Learn the fixed idiom second-class citizen, used to describe unequal or inferior treatment of a group within a society.
